review_notes: I read the whole 88-line file. Most proofs are one-line term proofs or simp calls. Three proofs share a destructuring pattern: `IsCover.mono`, `IsCover.mono_entourage` and `IsCover.union`. Each one unpacks `∃ y ∈ N, x ~[U] y` and rebuilds it with a changed witness membership or a changed relation. That is routine unfolding, not repeated nontrivial reasoning. A shared helper would not be shorter or clearer than the current one-liners. `IsCover.of_maximal_isSeparated` is the only proof with real content, and no other proof in the file repeats its argument. I did not search the rest of Mathlib for duplicates outside this file, because the rubric concerns repetition across proofs and none in this file qualifies.
